texts.facts: The sample was sent to Food Analyst and the Food Analyst vide his report bearing No. FSS/1011/2017 dated 10.10.2017 opined that the sample is misbranded on account of violation of Regulation No. 2.3.2 of The Food Safety and Standards (Packaging and Labelling) Regulations, 2011 ["FSS (P&L) Regulations" in short]. The Food Analyst reported that the Batch No. & Date of Packaging are not given on the Principal Display Panel of the tin container, which is in violation of Regulation 2.3.2 of FSS (P&L) Regulations. The FSO filed a complaint before the Ld.ADM, New Delhi under 3.1.1(3) of The Food Safety and Standards Rules, 2011("FSS Rules" in short) against the appellants for the adjudication of the offences under Sections 26(1) & 26(2)(ii) read with Section 3(1)(zf)(A)(i)(a), 3(1)(zf)(C)(i) and 3(1)(zf)(C)(iii) of FSS Act along with violation of Regulation No.2.2.2.8, 2.2.2.9 and 2.3.2 of FSS (P&L) Regulations. Before the Adjudicating Officer, the respondents/appellants herein submitted that the sampled commodity was manufactured and packed by M/s Banaskhantha District Coop. Milk Producers Union Ltd. and the remaining respondents had purchased it through valid bill and they are entitled to benefit of guarantee under Section 26(4) of the Act as sample commodity was taken into the same condition as was FSAT No. 01/20 Suresh Chand Ors. Vs. FSO, FSAT No. 02/20 Vikas Guleria Anr Vs. FSO & FSAT No. 03/20 D.T. Patel Anr Vs. FSO Page No. 5 of 16 being supplied. The respondents/appellants herein had also claimed the benefit of due diligence under Section 80 of FSS Act. The Adjudicating Officer after taking into account the averments of the respondents/appellants herein reached to the conclusion that respondents have violated the provisions of the FSS Act as well the Regulations contained in the FSS (P&L) Regulations and imposed the penalty under Section 52 of the FSS Act. 3. Aggrieved by the impugned order, the appellants have filed the aforesaid separate appeals. The appeal bearing FSAT No. 01/20 has been filed by Sh. Suresh Chand, FBOcum Proprietor of M/s Krishna Store & Sh. Aman Gupta and Sh. Amit Gupta, both partners of the supplier firm M/s Durga Agencies. The appeal bearing FSAT No. 02/20 has been filed by Distributor Company M/s Gujarat Coop Milk Marketing Federation Ltd. through its nominee Sh. Vikash Guleria and appeal bearing FSAT No. 03/20 has been filed by the manufacturing company M/s Banaskantha District Coop. on 2 September, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105554952/ 3 Milk Producers Union Ltd. through its nominee Sh. D.T. Patel. 4. In appeal bearing FSAT No. 01/20, the impugned order has been assailed on the ground that the Adjudicating Officer has passed the impugned order in a mechanical manner without appreciating that there was sufficient compliance of FSAT No. 01/20 Suresh Chand Ors. Vs. FSO, FSAT No. 02/20 Vikas Guleria Anr Vs. FSO & FSAT No. 03/20 D.T. Patel Anr Vs. FSO Page No. 6 of 16 Regulation 2.3.2 of the FSS (P&L) Regulations as on the Principal Display Panel which is defined as part of container / package, it was specifically mentioned that "FOR MAXIMUM RETAIL PRICE (INCLUSIVE OF ALL TAXES), BATCH NO./MELT NO., DATE OF PACKAGING, SEE BOTTOM / BODY OF THE TIN". It has been submitted that there was no violation of the said Regulation. Appellants have also submitted that the Adjudicating Officer failed to take into account the order/advisory dated 17.07.2018 whereby the Food Safety & Standards Authority of India has advised all the Commissioners of Food Safety not to initiate adjudication proceedings against Food Business Operator(s) for labeling defects of insignificant nature which could be easily rectified. The Commissioners were advised to take action under Section 32 of the Act in cases involving minor labeling defects which do not endanger food safety. The appellant also submitted that the sanction granted by the Sanctioning Authority was also not relating to the violation as per report of the Food Analyst. The plea of the appellant is that there is no violation of Section 3(1)(zf)(C)(i) of FSS Act. It was also submitted that there is violation of the mandatory provision of Section 47 of the Act while taking the sample from the FBO. The impugned order was also assailed on the ground that the FSAT No. 01/20 Suresh Chand Ors. Vs. FSO, FSAT No. 02/20 Vikas Guleria Anr Vs. FSO & FSAT No. 03/20 D.T. Patel Anr Vs. FSO Page No. 7 of 16 Food Analyst was neither the recognised nor any opportunity was granted as per Section 43 of the FSS Act. Similarly, the notice was not given to all the respondents/appellants herein to exercise their right under Section 46(4) of the FSS Act for challenging the report of the Food Analyst. The appellants also took a plea that the respondents/appellants herein were entitled to the benefit of guarantee and due diligence under Section 26 and 80(B)(2) of the FSS Act, 2006. The grounds taken in all the aforesaid three appeals are almost identical.
texts.arguments: The impugned order was also assailed on the ground that no public witness was joined and even if the case of the department is taken as it is, no prejudice was caused to the general public. Briefly stating, the plea of the appellants are that there is no violation of Regulation 2.3.2 of FSS (P&L) Regulations as all the material particulars were duly printed on the bottom of the tin container and on the Principal Display Panel, it was specifically mentioned that all these particulars are printed on the bottom of the tin container. It has been submitted that there was sufficient compliance of Regulation 2.3.2. of the FSS (P&L) Regulations. The appellants have submitted that Regulation 2.3.2 of FSS FSAT No. 01/20 Suresh Chand Ors. Vs. FSO, FSAT No. 02/20 Vikas Guleria Anr Vs. FSO & FSAT No. 03/20 D.T. Patel Anr Vs. FSO Page No. 8 of 16 (P&L) Regulation also empowers to give all these information on "another place" and therefore, it is not mandatory to give all these information on the Principal Display Panel. The appellants have relied upon Hindustan Lever Ltd. Ors. Vs. Food Inspector 2007(1) 299 and R. Chandramohan Vs. FSO 2019(1) FAC 547 Madras. In the Written Submission, it has been submitted that there is a clear violation of Regulations 2.3.2, 2.2.2.(8)&(9) of FSS (P&L) Regulations. It has been submitted that admittedly, the information were not given on the Principal Display Panel and instead, has been given on the bottom of the body of the container. Ld. Chief PP for the State has further submitted that contentions of the appellants that the practice of furnishing information regarding Batch No., Date of Packaging at the bottom of the tin container is a regular business practice and is largely followed by the Food Industry, cannot be accepted. It has been submitted that providing information in such a manner would mislead the consumers at large and as per the Regulations, nothing comes in the way of the appellants to print such information on the Principal Display Panel of the tin container. Ld. Chief PP for the State has submitted that it is a settled FSAT No. 01/20 Suresh Chand Ors. Vs. FSO, FSAT No. 02/20 Vikas Guleria Anr Vs. FSO & FSAT No. 03/20 D.T. Patel Anr Vs. FSO Page No. 9 of 16 proposition that where the language of the Act is clear and explicit, it must be given effect to it. It has further been submitted that the Designated Officer has given the proper sanction on the basis of the facts of the case. It has been submitted that on the basis of the report of the Food Analyst, the provisions for misleading, deception and nonlabeling in accordance with the requirement of the Act or the regulations were also attracted. It has also been submitted that FBO was given due opportunity for sending the report to the Accredited Laboratory, which is evident from the Panchnama prepared by the FSO at the time of taking the sample. It has also been submitted that M/s Gujarat Coop Milk Marketing Federation Ltd. was issued due notice for preferring an appeal under Section 46(4) of the Act for reanalysis of the sample and therefore, there was no need to issue a separate notice to its nominee. Ld. Chief PP for the State has further submitted that under Section 26 & 26(2) of the FSS Act, the FBO is under a duty to ensure that the articles of food satisfy the requirements of the Act and Regulations made thereunder at all stages of sale. It has been submitted that no FBO shall sell any article of food which is misbranded. The FBO is required to take reasonable precautions and due diligence to prevent the commission of the offence. 12. Section 23 of the Act specifically provides that no person shall manufacture, distribute, sell or expose for sale or despatch or deliver to any agent or broker for the purpose of sale, any packaged food products which are not marked and labelled in the manner as may be specified by regulations.
